standard_prerequisites.name: Functorial injective embeddings of modules
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies, for every ring and module over it, a functorial injective embedding of the module into an injective module.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pointwise products of sheaves

standard_prerequisites.name: Injectivity detected on stalks

standard_prerequisites.use: Supply that a map of sheaves of modules is injective when it is so on stalks, and that a sheaf constructed stalkwise from injective modules is injective.

core_obligations: The construction (proof lines 722-742): for a sheaf of modules the author forms the assignment sending an open set to the product over its points of the functorial injective hull of the stalk at that point, notes that it is a sheaf of modules by the cited examples, and defines the canonical map from the given sheaf into it by taking germs at each point.

Injectivity of the map (proof lines 742-746): the canonical map is injective because injectivity of a map of sheaves of modules can be checked on stalks and the maps on stalks are the chosen injections.

Injectivity of the target and functoriality (proof lines 746-764): the constructed sheaf is injective because it is built stalkwise from injective modules, and both the construction and the map are functorial in the given sheaf, which gives functorial injective embeddings and hence enough injectives.
proof_roadmap: Choose functorial injective hulls of the stalk modules and take their product over the points of each open set.
Check that this assignment is a sheaf of modules and that the germ map is injective on stalks.
Use the stalkwise description of injectivity to conclude, and observe functoriality.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that the category of sheaves of modules on a ringed space has enough injectives and in fact functorial injective embeddings (statement lines 714-720). The proof is a complete argument: the assignment sending an open set to the product over its points of functorial injective hulls of the stalks is shown to be a sheaf of modules and to receive an injective canonical map from the given sheaf, using that injectivity can be checked on stalks (proof lines 722-746); and the constructed sheaf is injective because it is built stalkwise from injective modules, with functoriality giving the stronger statement (proof lines 746-764). The non-formal content is the stalkwise construction and the injectivity check. The claim is H2.
